subject: biology
source_note: Topic structure follows the IB Diploma Biology guide (first assessment 2025), organised by its four themes across levels of organisation. Theme names are guide-accurate; connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (the IB does not publish these).

units.name: Theme A — Unity & Diversity
units.blurb: Molecules, cells, organisms and ecosystems that share and vary

units.name: Theme B — Form & Function
units.blurb: How structure relates to function at every level

units.name: Theme C — Interaction & Interdependence
units.blurb: Signalling, interactions and systems working together

topics.name: Molecules (Water & Carbon Compounds)
topics.blurb: Water, carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids

topics.name: Cells & Origins
topics.blurb: Cell structure, origin of cells and cell specialisation

topics.name: Ecosystems & Biomes
topics.blurb: Communities, biomes and the variety of ecosystems

topics.name: Membranes & Membrane Transport
topics.blurb: Membrane structure, transport and cell signalling basics

topics.name: Gas Exchange & Transport
topics.blurb: Exchange surfaces, transport systems and SA:V ratio

topics.name: Form & Function in Organisms
topics.blurb: Adaptations of plants and animals to their roles

topics.name: Cell & Organism Signalling
topics.blurb: Hormones, nerves, homeostasis and the immune system

topics.name: Interactions in Communities
topics.blurb: Feeding relationships, nutrient cycling and populations

topics.name: Reproduction & Cell Division
topics.blurb: Meiosis, sexual reproduction and the cell cycle

topics.name: Inheritance & Gene Expression
topics.blurb: DNA, genes, inheritance and gene expression

topics.name: Evolution & Biodiversity Change
topics.blurb: Natural selection, speciation and evidence for evolution

connections.why: The properties of lipids and proteins explain membrane structure
Proteins act as the enzymes that drive metabolism
Cells arise from pre-existing cells by division
Membrane receptors underpin cell signalling and homeostasis
Gas exchange supplies oxygen for aerobic respiration
Photosynthesis fixes the energy flowing through communities
Coordinated signalling enables organisms' adapted functions
Meiosis and reproduction pass on and reshuffle genes
Heritable variation is the basis of natural selection
The diversity of organisms is the product of evolution
Disrupting interactions drives change in ecosystems
Ecosystems change through succession and human impact
Specialised cells build the structures organisms need
Gene expression controls which enzymes a cell makes
